title: TrackFlow Telemetry Event Schemas
description: Canonical event catalogue for TrackFlow telemetry. Every event is wrapped in the standard envelope; event-specific fields live under properties.

envelope.description: Standard envelope for every TrackFlow telemetry event.

eventId.description: Unique identifier of this event instance.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the event occurred.

sessionId.description: User session identifier for the same journey.

userId.description: Stable internal user identifier of the acting user.

schemaVersion.description: Semver of the event schema used to produce the payload.

requestId.description: Correlation ID for the backend request or trace.

properties.description: Event-specific payload defined by the event allowlist.

inbound_order_created.description: A new inbound order (stock receipt) was created for a client's SKU at a warehouse.
inbound_order_created.hypothesis: We need to understand how stock enters each warehouse, by client and category.
inbound_order_created.decision: Forecast receiving capacity and staffing needs.
inbound_order_created.business_justification: This event records inbound stock movement at the ledger level, which supports receiving analysis, capacity planning, and operational forecasting.
inbound_order_created.sensitive_handling: No carrier, recipient, or credential material is collected. Only opaque internal identifiers are used.

outbound_order_created.description: A new outbound order (stock dispatch) was created for a client's SKU at a warehouse.
outbound_order_created.hypothesis: We need to know outbound velocity by warehouse, client, and category.
outbound_order_created.decision: Prioritize replenishment planning and picking resources.
outbound_order_created.business_justification: Batch-level dispatch telemetry supports demand analysis and operational planning without exposing carrier or recipient details.
outbound_order_created.sensitive_handling: No carrier data or recipient/end-consumer personal data is collected. `destination_type` is an internal classification only.

stock_threshold_triggered.description: A SKU's stock level crossed a configured minimum threshold at a warehouse.
stock_threshold_triggered.hypothesis: We need to know when a SKU is near or below the inventory floor threshold.
stock_threshold_triggered.decision: Trigger replenishment before fulfillment is disrupted.
stock_threshold_triggered.business_justification: Stockout-risk signals need near-real-time visibility so replenishment teams can act before service disruption occurs.
stock_threshold_triggered.sensitive_handling: No personal data is collected; only warehouse, client, product, and threshold metadata are logged.

direct_stock_edit_rejected.description: An attempt to modify stock directly (bypassing InboundOrder/OutboundOrder) was rejected.
direct_stock_edit_rejected.hypothesis: We need to detect and quantify attempts to bypass the approved inventory workflow.
direct_stock_edit_rejected.decision: Enforce process controls and access restrictions when direct stock edits are attempted.
direct_stock_edit_rejected.business_justification: This is a security and integrity event that must be surfaced promptly to control misuse and protect inventory accuracy.
direct_stock_edit_rejected.sensitive_handling: No personal identifiers beyond an internal stable user ID are included. No credentials or tokens are recorded.

inventory_discrepancy_detected.description: A stock reconciliation or audit process detected a mismatch between expected and counted stock for a SKU.
inventory_discrepancy_detected.hypothesis: We need to understand where and how often expected stock diverges from actual stock.
inventory_discrepancy_detected.decision: Prioritize audits and root-cause analysis for reconciliation issues.
inventory_discrepancy_detected.business_justification: Reconciliation mismatches are evaluated in audit cycles and operational reporting rather than as immediate per-event alerts.
inventory_discrepancy_detected.sensitive_handling: No personal data, carrier metadata, or recipient details are included.

inventory_count_recorded.description: A physical inventory count for a SKU is recorded during an audit or cycle count.
inventory_count_recorded.hypothesis: We need to know which SKUs are actually being physically counted and how frequently audit coverage occurs.
inventory_count_recorded.decision: Prioritize audit schedules and warehouse resources for SKUs or locations that are not being counted frequently enough.
inventory_count_recorded.business_justification: This event records a physical inventory count taken during an audit or cycle count. It does not modify stock and supports warehouse audit coverage analysis.
inventory_count_recorded.sensitive_handling: No personal or carrier data is collected. Only audit context and inventory identifiers are retained.

user_login_succeeded.hypothesis: We need to understand usage patterns and access volume across internal users.
user_login_succeeded.decision: Right-size licensing and detect unusual access patterns.
user_login_succeeded.business_justification: This gives a usage baseline for monitoring access patterns and changes in system adoption.
user_login_succeeded.sensitive_handling: The event records only the authentication method and optional site context. No password, token, or credential material is collected.

user_login_failed.hypothesis: We need to detect repeated failed authentication attempts and potential attack patterns.
user_login_failed.decision: Trigger lockout workflows and security review.
user_login_failed.business_justification: Failed logins are a near-real-time security signal that should be examined quickly to prevent brute force or takeover attempts.
user_login_failed.sensitive_handling: No credentials, tokens, or raw password values are recorded.

permission_denied.description: An action was attempted without the required authorization.
permission_denied.hypothesis: We need to measure authorization failures and identify misconfigured roles or probing attempts.
permission_denied.decision: Adjust role policy or investigate suspicious behavior.
permission_denied.business_justification: Permission denials are a security signal and should be visible quickly for operational review.
permission_denied.sensitive_handling: No user names, address details, or credential material are stored.

api_request_failed.description: A backend API request returned an error after retries were exhausted.
api_request_failed.hypothesis: We need to identify which API surfaces fail most often and under what conditions.
api_request_failed.decision: Prioritize endpoint reliability fixes and infrastructure investments.
api_request_failed.business_justification: API failures require prompt detection to support incident response and reliable service operations.
api_request_failed.sensitive_handling: No request payload or user content is logged. Only route and status metadata are retained.

background_job_failed.description: A scheduled background job failed to complete.
background_job_failed.hypothesis: We need to know which scheduled or asynchronous jobs fail and how frequently.
background_job_failed.decision: Prioritize fixes to the jobs protecting stock accuracy and operational integrity.
background_job_failed.business_justification: Scheduled job failures are operationally important but generally reviewed in aggregate rather than processed as a per-event real-time alert.
background_job_failed.sensitive_handling: No personal data or credentials are recorded.

page_load_measured.description: A backoffice page finished loading and recorded its load duration.
page_load_measured.hypothesis: We need to know which screens are slowest for internal users.
page_load_measured.decision: Prioritize front-end optimization on the pages with the worst performance.
page_load_measured.business_justification: Performance trends are gathered in aggregate and sampled to manage volume while preserving visibility into slow pages.
page_load_measured.sensitive_handling: No user content, personal identifiers, or raw URLs with query parameters are stored.

search_query_executed.description: A user executed a search or filter in the backoffice.
search_query_executed.hypothesis: We need to know how users search for inventory and operational data, without collecting the raw query text.
search_query_executed.decision: Improve search UX and indexing for the most common query patterns.
search_query_executed.business_justification: Search telemetry supports product UX decisions and indexing improvements while avoiding incidental PII capture.
search_query_executed.sensitive_handling: Raw free-text queries are not recorded. Only context and result metrics are captured.

backoffice_page_viewed.description: A user navigated to a backoffice screen.
backoffice_page_viewed.hypothesis: We need to understand which backoffice screens are used most often and where users spend time.
backoffice_page_viewed.decision: Prioritize UX and process changes based on actual adoption patterns.
backoffice_page_viewed.business_justification: High-volume page-view telemetry is best handled in aggregated batches and debounced to preserve signal while limiting noise.
backoffice_page_viewed.sensitive_handling: No names, emails, or URL parameters with user data are recorded.

order_creation_abandoned.description: A user started creating an inbound or outbound order but left before submission.
order_creation_abandoned.hypothesis: We need to identify where users abandon order creation flows.
order_creation_abandoned.decision: Reduce friction in the creation process and improve conversion at the abandonment point.
order_creation_abandoned.business_justification: Funnel analysis is aggregated and reviewed in batches rather than as a real-time operational alert.
order_creation_abandoned.sensitive_handling: No recipient or carrier details are included.

report_export_requested.description: A user requested an export of inventory or order data from the backoffice.
report_export_requested.hypothesis: We need to know which reports are exported most often by internal users.
report_export_requested.decision: Prioritize native dashboard or export feature investment based on actual demand.
report_export_requested.business_justification: Export usage is a reporting and product-usage signal rather than a real-time operational event.
report_export_requested.sensitive_handling: The event records only the request metadata, not the exported file contents or customer data.
